question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
sql:
WITH monthly_balances AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM CAST(txn_date AS DATE)) as month_num,
        SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) as total_deposits,
        SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) as total_withdrawals
    FROM customer_transactions
    WHERE txn_date LIKE '2020%'
    GROUP BY customer_id, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM CAST(txn_date AS DATE))
),
customer_month_balances AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        month_num,
        total_deposits - total_withdrawals as month_end_balance
    FROM monthly_balances
),
monthly_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        month_num,
        SUM(CASE WHEN month_end_balance > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as positive_count,
        AVG(month_end_balance) as avg_balance
    FROM customer_month_balances
    GROUP BY month_num
),
highest_month AS (
    SELECT month_num, avg_balance
    FROM monthly_stats
    WHERE positive_count = (SELECT MAX(positive_count) FROM monthly_stats)
),
lowest_month AS (
    SELECT month_num, avg_balance
    FROM monthly_stats
    WHERE positive_count = (SELECT MIN(positive_count) FROM monthly_stats)
)
SELECT 
    h.avg_balance - l.avg_balance as balance_difference
FROM highest_month h, lowest_month l
